en: In this app here, we allow users to attach
images to posts. And of course, on the
frontend, we show those images.
And I wanna show optimized versions of these
images. So what I'm doing here on the
backend is I'm using the Bun Image API to
get a file from R2 using the file method
supported by Bun's S3 client to get hold of
a file.
And then
thankfully Bun automatically supports using
such a remote stored file,
S3 stored file as input for its image API.
So we can call image on that and I set up
some maximum dimensions I expect that image
to have.
Then I call the resize method supported by
Bun's image API
to set a specific width
and height, which is the same because I
wanna get a square image.
The fit I set to inside to avoid stretching.
And then I convert everything to a WebP
format image. So no matter what the user
uploaded, if it was a PNG or a JPEG, I
convert it to a WebP
and then I
return this as a blob using the standard
blob API. That is what optimizeImage on the
backend does.
Now where is this being called? It's called
in images.ts
and images.ts is just another route
registration file where I register one route
a route for
serving an image, for returning an image,
and that route is called from the frontend
whenever the image should be displayed.
And in that image route or in that route
handler,
I get hold of my storage object here,
which is just that object I'm constructing
here in the r2.ts file.
Then I'm getting my image data here from
that uploads folder.
Then I see which width was requested because
actually the client can request different
widths for example, for mobile and
desktop screens.
And then I get that image blob here, as you
see, by calling that optimizeImage method I
just showed you. That is what's happening
here. And then that blob is returned as a
response with some caching headers to make
sure it can be cached efficiently.
And that response therefore then contains
the optimized image, which is then the
actual image that will be rendered and shown
on the client. Therefore, my R2 bucket is
still private. Nobody has access to it
except for these temporary upload presigned
URLs.
But the images can still be served since the
serving logic goes through my Bun backend
API where I then also optimize them. And
that optimization happens using the Bun
Image API, another amazing feature built
into Bun.
